case_name: Dr. P. Nalla Thamby Thera v Union Of India And Others
facts: The petitioner is a resident of Sultanbattery area in the State of Kerala and describes himself as a commuter of the Indian Railways.

He has alleged violation of fundamental rights guaranteed under arts. 19 and 21 and claims reliefs of mandamus to the Union of India for implementing the reports of the Kunzru, Wanchoo and Sikri Committees, appointing a fact finding Commission to inquire and report about the numerous train accidents from 1970 onwards and for several other directions to the Union Government and the instrumentalities connected with the administration of the Railways.

The Indian Railways Act, 1890 ('Act' for short) has prescribed several safety measures; based upon experience, the Railway Board through which apex body the administration is run and controlled has also prescribed rules and issued instructions which are not being properly implemented.
issues: Whether the recommendations of the Accidents Enquiry Committees were examined and implemented within the limits of financial and material resources.
Whether the unmanned level crossings are gradually being replaced by manned ones and improved technical gadgets are being provided for efficient operation.
Whether the State Governments appeared to be aware of their responsibilities in this matter and about 2/3 of the funds of the Safety Works had been utilised by March 31, 1982.
petitioner_arguments: The recommendations of the Accidents Enquiry Committees were not examined and implemented within the limits of financial and material resources.
Unmanned level crossings are gradually being replaced by manned ones and improved technical gadgets are not being provided for efficient operation.
The State Governments appeared to be unaware of their responsibilities in this matter and less than 2/3 of the funds of the Safety Works had been utilised by March 31, 1982.
respondent_arguments: The recommendations of the Accidents Enquiry Committees were examined and implemented within the limits of financial and material resources.
Unmanned level crossings are gradually being replaced by manned ones and improved technical gadgets are being provided for efficient operation.
The State Governments appeared to be aware of their responsibilities in this matter and about 2/3 of the funds of the Safety Works had been utilised by March 31, 1982.
holding: The Railways are a public utility service run on monopoly basis and should not be run merely as a commercial venture with a view to making profits.
The services should be prompt, efficient and dignified.
Facilities in running trains should be ensured.
Quality of accommodation and availability thereof should be ensured.
Stringent laws should be made and strictly enforced to free the Railways from ticketless travelling.
Security both to the travelling public as also to the non-travelling citizens must be provided.
The obligations cast by the Railways Act and the Rules under it must be complied with.
